props.text: The terms for using this website, requesting a consultation and using the tools we link to.
Eligibility and use of the Site
These Terms of Service (“Terms”) govern your use of the website operated by Westlake Medical Aesthetics (“we,” “us” or “our”) at westlaketxmedspa.com (the “Site”).

By using the Site, sending us information, requesting a consultation or contacting us electronically, you agree to these Terms. If you don’t agree, please don’t use the Site. We may update these Terms from time to time. When we do, we will post the new version here with a new effective date. If you keep using the Site after that, you accept the updated Terms.
Eligibility and use of the Site
You must be at least 18 years old, or have a parent or legal guardian involved, to request a consultation or send us information through the Site.
You agree to use the Site only for lawful purposes, and not in any way that interferes with how it works, its security, or its accessibility for others.

The Site gives general information about our practice, our treatments, how often they are usually repeated and how to pay for them. Everything on it is for general information and education only. It does not replace an in-person assessment, a diagnosis or a treatment plan from a licensed medical provider.
Using the Site does not make you our patient. That relationship starts only when our office accepts you as a patient and you receive care from our medical providers.

What the Site says about who a treatment suits, how long results take to show, how long they last and how much downtime to expect is general. Your own suitability and plan can only be decided at a consultation.
If you have a medical emergency, including a reaction after a treatment, call 911 or your local emergency number. Don’t rely on the Site, email or social media messages for urgent care.

You can ask for a consultation through the Site, in person or by video. Sending a request does not guarantee an appointment. An appointment is confirmed only after our office checks availability and contacts you.

You agree to give us accurate, current and complete information. We may change, reschedule or decline a request because of our providers’ availability, scheduling conflicts, missing information, whether the treatment is clinically appropriate for you, or other reasonable considerations.
If you ask for a video consultation or send us photos, you confirm that you have the right to share those images.

A virtual consultation gives a preliminary, non-diagnostic opinion only. It does not replace an in-person assessment. Any recommendation made by video may change once one of our providers has seen you in person, and treatment is only given after that.

Website forms, email and social media messages are for routine questions and appointment requests. Please don’t send sensitive medical or financial information through them. For anything involving your health information, call our office or use a secure channel we give you.

When you give us your contact details, you agree that we can contact you by phone, voicemail and email about your request, your appointments and your treatment. This includes confirmations and reminders, aftercare instructions and follow-ups. We will only send you marketing if you have agreed to receive it, and you can stop it at any time.

Email and other electronic messages are not always fully secure and can be intercepted. Please keep that in mind before you share sensitive information that way. Information you give us as a patient is governed by our Notice of Privacy Practices under HIPAA, which you can get at our office or by asking us.

Our contact form has a checkbox for text messages. If you tick it and give us your mobile number, you are agreeing to receive text messages from Westlake Medical Aesthetics at that number: appointment confirmations and reminders, aftercare follow-ups, replies from our team, and news or offers if you have agreed to those.

Ticking the box is not a condition of being treated here. You may reply STOP to any message to stop them, and HELP for help. How often we text depends on your appointments. Message and data rates may apply. Mobile carriers are not liable for messages that arrive late or not at all.

By ticking the box you confirm that the number is yours, or that you are allowed to enrol it. Text messages are not secure, so please don’t send sensitive information that way. How we handle your number is set out in our
The Site links to financing offered by independent companies, such as Cherry and CareCredit. That financing is provided by those companies, not by Westlake Medical Aesthetics.

We don’t control approvals, application results, credit requirements, payment terms, lending terms or promotions. Please take any questions about a financing decision, account or payment to the financing company.
Treatment prices are confirmed at your consultation, before you agree to any treatment.

The membership described on the Site is a summary. Joining requires a signed membership agreement, and that agreement sets out the monthly fee, the minimum commitment, the notice needed to cancel, what is included and how your membership balance works. If the Site and your signed agreement ever differ, the agreement applies.
When you use the Site or contact our office, you agree to:
Give true, accurate and complete information, including contact details that belong to you
Use the Site only for genuine personal or patient purposes
Not send false, misleading or unauthorized requests, including requests made on behalf of someone who hasn’t agreed to it
Not try to disrupt, damage, disable, reverse engineer or gain unauthorized access to the Site or any connected service
Tell us if your contact details change and you still want to hear from us about your appointments

Everything on the Site, including text, graphics, logos, icons, photographs, before-and-after images, videos, page layouts and design, is owned by or licensed to Westlake Medical Aesthetics and protected by intellectual property laws.

You may not copy, reproduce, republish, distribute, change, display, transmit or otherwise use anything from the Site without our written permission. The exception is limited personal, non-commercial use, such as printing a page for your own reference.

Product and brand names mentioned on the Site, such as Botox, Xeomin, Dysport, Jeuveau, Sculptra, Morpheus8, SkinPen and HydraFacial, are trademarks of their respective owners. We use them only to describe the treatments we offer.

Some features and links on the Site are provided by other companies, including the booking and contact form and the customer relationship system behind it (Go High Level / LeadConnector), financing providers, Google Maps, Google reviews, Instagram and TikTok, and the platform used for video consultations. The Site also links to Stone Surgical Arts, which is a separate practice. These companies have their own terms and privacy policies, and a link does not mean we endorse or control them. We are not responsible for their availability, accuracy, content, security or practices.

Nothing on the Site is medical advice, and you should not rely on it instead of professional care. Results vary from person to person. Before-and-after photos and reviews show the results of particular patients. They do not promise or guarantee what your results will be. Always talk to a licensed medical provider about your diagnosis, treatment options and care.

The Site and its content are provided “as is” and “as available,” without warranties of any kind, express or implied. This includes warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy and non-infringement.

props.text: What we collect when you use this website, why we collect it, who we share it with and the choices you have.

Westlake Medical Aesthetics (“we,” “us” or “our”) respects your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we handle the personal information you share with us through our website, westlaketxmedspa.com (the “Site”), and when you contact us by phone or email.

This policy covers information collected through the Site. Information you give us as a patient while receiving care is governed by our separate Notice of Privacy Practices under HIPAA. You can get a copy at our office or by asking us.
We collect the information you choose to give us, for example when you:
Request a consultation, in person or by video
Ask about a treatment, our membership or financing
Send us photos ahead of a virtual consultation
Fill in patient forms before your first visit
Call us, email us or message us on social media
This can include your name, email address, phone number, mailing address, date of birth, the concerns and goals you describe, and anything else you decide to tell us.
When you visit the Site, we and our service providers may automatically collect some information about your device and how you use the Site, including:
Your IP address and approximate location
Browser type, operating system and device identifiers
Pages visited, time spent on them and the page that sent you here
Information from cookies and similar technologies (see section 07)

If you send photos of your face or skin, or describe a concern, we handle that information with the same care as any patient health information. Please don’t send detailed medical histories or other sensitive health information through website forms, social media messages or unencrypted email. For anything sensitive, call us on
We use the information we collect to:
Answer your questions and schedule consultations and appointments
Assess whether a treatment suits you, prepare your treatment plan and coordinate your care
Provide the treatments you ask for
Send appointment confirmations and reminders, aftercare instructions and follow-ups
Set up and manage your membership, if you join
Take payments and help you with financing options
Send news about treatments and offers, but only if you have agreed to receive it
Improve the Site, our services and your experience with us
Meet our legal, regulatory and professional obligations

Our contact form has a checkbox for text messages. If you tick it and give us your mobile number, you agree to receive text messages from us at that number. Ticking it is not a condition of being treated here, and you can ask us to stop at any time.

We do not sell or share your mobile number or your consent to be texted with anyone for their own marketing. We share it only with the providers that send the messages for us, and only so the message reaches you.
Text messages are not a secure channel. Please don’t send health, financial or other sensitive information by text.
We do not sell or rent your personal information. We share it only when we need to run the practice and look after you, including with:
Service providers that support the Site, our contact form, scheduling, communications, payments and analytics, under agreements that limit how they can use your information
Financing companies, when you ask to apply for financing through them
Other healthcare providers involved in your care, including a practice we refer you to, if you ask us to or agree to it
Legal and regulatory authorities, when the law or a subpoena requires it, or to protect rights, property or safety
If the practice is ever sold, merged or restructured, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction, as the law allows.
Some features of the Site are provided by other companies. These may include:
Our booking and contact form, and the customer relationship system behind it, provided by Go High Level (LeadConnector). What you type into that form is sent to them and stored there for us.
Financing providers such as Cherry and CareCredit, whose applications you complete on their own websites
Google Maps, for directions to our office
Google Business Profile, where our patient reviews are published
Instagram and TikTok, where we post updates
A video platform for virtual consultations
Web analytics services, such as Google Analytics, that show us how visitors use the Site
These companies may collect information about you under their own privacy policies, and we encourage you to read them.

If you join our membership, we collect the details needed to enrol you, charge the recurring payment and keep your account up to date. Card payments are handled by our payment processor, and we don’t store full card numbers on the Site. The terms of your membership are set out in the membership agreement you sign.
A cookie is a small data file saved on your device when you visit a website. We and our service providers may use cookies and similar technologies to:
Keep the Site working and secure
Understand how visitors find and use the Site
You can control cookies in your browser settings. If you turn them off, parts of the Site may not work properly.
Stop marketing emails by clicking “unsubscribe” in any email, or by contacting us.
Ask to see, correct or delete the personal information we hold about you by contacting us (see section 13).
Change your cookie settings in your browser.

Depending on where you live, you may have more rights under laws such as the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act or the California Consumer Privacy Act. To use those rights, contact us. We will reply within the time the law requires, and we will not treat you differently for using them.
Your medical record is governed by HIPAA and Texas law, which may limit our ability to delete or change clinical records.

We use administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect your personal information. However, no website, internet transmission or electronic storage is completely secure. To protect yourself, please don’t send confidential health information through website forms, social media or unencrypted email.

We keep personal information for as long as we need it for the purposes in this policy, to meet our legal and professional obligations, to resolve disputes and to enforce our agreements. Medical records are kept for as long as Texas law and the Texas Medical Board require.

The Site is not intended for children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you think a child has sent us information through the Site, contact us and we will delete it.

The Site links to websites we don’t control, including our social media profiles, review sites, our financing partners and Stone Surgical Arts, a separate practice. We are not responsible for their content or their privacy practices, so please read their policies before you share information with them.

cells.title: About Us | Westlake Medical Aesthetics

props.text: We'll walk you through every option, from non-invasive treatments with our team to surgery with our sister practice, and build a treatment plan around what you want and what your skin needs.

Westlake Medical Aesthetics is its own practice, with its own medical aesthetics team. Surgery is done by a separate surgical team at our sister practice, Stone Surgical Arts. If your provider thinks surgery would give you a better result, they'll tell you and refer you.
Every new patient is assessed by our highly skilled medical providers before any treatment is planned.
We keep first treatments conservative and check in at two weeks. Adding a little more is easy.
No two plans are the same. We take your goals seriously and talk through every option with you at your consultation.
One private office off Highway 114 with parking at the door: a front desk, a consultation room and treatment rooms.

cells.title: Dr. Mona Stone, DDS | Westlake Medical Aesthetics

props.text: A board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon at Stone Surgical Arts, our sister practice. Dr. Stone doesn't treat patients at Westlake Medical Aesthetics; our nurse practitioner and esthetician do.
Oral and maxillofacial surgery covers the bones of the face and jaw and the tissue over them. It's the foundation of her surgical work.
Surgery happens at Stone Surgical Arts.
Facelifts, neck lifts, eyelid surgery and other procedures that need an incision are done at Stone Surgical Arts.
We'll tell you if surgery makes sense.
Past a certain point, injectables can't do what surgery can. If that's where you are, our providers will say so and can refer you to Dr. Stone.
Start small, then review at two weeks.
Adding a little more at a follow-up takes a few minutes. Waiting for too much to wear off takes months. That's why our providers keep first treatments conservative.

cells.title: Botox & Xeomin in Westlake, TX | Westlake Medical Aesthetics

props.text: About fifteen minutes, no anesthetic and no downtime. Placed by our nurse practitioner, who usually starts with fewer units than you'd expect.
Pricing depends on the number of units and the areas treated. You'll get a quote at your consultation.

Botox and Xeomin are both botulinum toxin type A, a purified protein that temporarily relaxes the muscle it's placed in. Small amounts in the upper face stop those muscles from creasing the skin, so the lines they cause soften.

It doesn't fill, tighten or remove anything. A line you can still see when your face is completely relaxed is etched into the skin, and Botox alone will only improve it slowly. That's the first thing your provider checks.
What it can do for you
Most people describe how they look rather than what they want done: tired, annoyed, older than they feel. In the upper face, that usually comes down to three muscles.
Forehead lines soften without dropping your brow.
The frown line between your eyebrows stops making you look cross.
Crow's feet ease when you smile.
A heavy brow can lift slightly when the muscle pulling it down relaxes.
Most healthy adults are good candidates. Your consultation is where we confirm that and work out how much you need. For a first treatment, it's usually less than you'd think.

You're pregnant or breastfeeding, have a neuromuscular condition, have an infection where you'd be treated, or your lines are static. In that last case, your provider may suggest a skin treatment or filler instead.

All four are botulinum toxin type A. They differ in how quickly they start, how far they spread and how they behave over years of treatment. Having all four means your provider can choose the one that suits you.
Most first treatments. It has the longest track record and is very predictable in small areas.
Patients whose Botox seems to wear off faster than it used to. Xeomin has no accessory proteins.
Larger areas like a broad forehead, where a wider spread helps.
Your Botox is placed by Brooke, our nurse practitioner injector, after a full assessment. She'll keep your first treatment conservative and see you again at two weeks to check the result.
If your doctor agrees, pause fish oil, vitamin E and high-dose anti-inflammatories for about a week. They can cause bruising.
Skip alcohol for 24 hours beforehand, for the same reason.
Come with a clean face if you can. We'll remove any makeup before we start.
Let us know about recent dental work, vaccinations or illness.
Stay upright for four hours. No lying flat or face-down naps.
Don't rub or massage the treated areas.
Avoid hard workouts, saunas and hot yoga for a day.
Small bumps settle within an hour. A bruise can take a few days.
Judge the result at two weeks, not three days. We'll book your follow-up then.
We're updating our before-and-after gallery. In the meantime, ask to see results for your treatment at your consultation.
The needle is very fine and each injection takes about a second. Most patients describe a quick sting. No anesthetic is needed, and you can drive yourself home.
How soon will I see it?
Movement starts to soften after three to seven days, and the full effect shows at about two weeks. We book your follow-up then.
Not if it's dosed and placed well. We treat the muscles that are creasing the skin and leave the rest working, and we keep first treatments conservative.
What happens when it wears off?
Your muscles gradually go back to how they worked before, and so do the lines. Nothing ends up worse than it was.
How many units will I need?
It depends on your muscles and the areas you want treated, so we can't say over the phone. You'll get your number and a quote after the assessment, before anything is injected.
For volume that has faded rather than lines from movement. Often done at the same visit.
A deep clean and hydration boost that pairs well with regular Botox.
A monthly facial plus 10% off treatments like Botox, if you come in regularly.

cells.title: Treatments | Westlake Medical Aesthetics, Westlake TX

props.text: Non-invasive treatments that soften lines, restore volume and help your skin make more of its own collagen, so you look your best without surgery. Open any treatment to see how long it takes, when you'll see results and how long they last.

Neuromodulators soften the lines that come from movement, fillers restore volume, and biostimulators like Sculptra help your skin build its own collagen over time. Every injection is done by our nurse practitioner.

Botox and Xeomin relax the muscles that crease the skin, softening forehead lines, frown lines and crow's feet. Xeomin has no accessory proteins, which can help if Botox seems to wear off faster than it used to.
Two more neuromodulators that work the same way as Botox. Dysport spreads a little further, which can suit a larger area like the forehead, and Jeuveau is often chosen for frown lines.
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.

Hyaluronic acid filler restores shape and volume to the lips, cheeks, chin and jawline, and can soften hollows under the eyes. Placement is planned around your facial structure so the result looks like you.
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.
Sculptra is a biostimulator. Instead of filling a space, it prompts your skin to rebuild collagen, so results appear gradually over a few months and can last two years or more.
Volume loss, Laxity & jawline, Texture & pores
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.
These treatments prompt your skin to repair and renew itself. Most are done as a short series, and results keep improving for a few months after the last session.

Radiofrequency energy delivered through fine microneedles tightens and smooths the deeper layers of the skin while leaving the surface largely intact. It works well on the jawline, the neck and acne scarring.
Laxity & jawline, Texture & pores, Acne scarring
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.

A peel lifts away damaged surface skin to even out tone, fade sun spots and refine texture. Light peels have almost no downtime, deeper ones need about a week, and we'll help you pick one that fits your schedule.
Pigmentation & tone, Texture & pores, Dryness & dullness
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.
SkinPen creates thousands of tiny channels in the skin, which starts its natural repair process and boosts collagen. It's a good fit for acne scars, enlarged pores and early fine lines.
Texture & pores, Acne scarring, Fine lines & wrinkles
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.
Regular facials keep skin clear, smooth and hydrated between treatments. Members get one every month as part of their plan.

Cleansing, exfoliation, extractions and hydration in a single treatment. We offer several versions, from 45 to 90 minutes, so your esthetician can match the facial to your skin, and you can go straight back to your day.
Texture & pores, Dryness & dullness, Pigmentation & tone
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.

Dermaplaning is a gentle exfoliation. Your esthetician glides a sterile blade across the skin to lift away dead surface cells and fine facial hair, the peach fuzz, leaving skin smoother and brighter. Makeup and skincare go on more evenly afterward.
Ask about this treatment at your consultation and we'll go through it with you.

Boosters are targeted serums added to your HydraFacial, chosen for what your skin needs that day, whether that's brightening, firming or extra hydration. They're infused during the facial, so there's nothing extra to book.

PRP uses a concentrate of your own platelets to support skin and hair. Results come on gradually, and nothing synthetic is involved.
A small amount of your blood is drawn and spun to concentrate the platelets, which are then returned to the skin. It's a good choice if you'd rather avoid fillers or synthetic products.

PRP injected into the scalp to support thinning hair. It works best on follicles that are still active, so starting early tends to give better results.
